Marcus Hale, the chief financial officer of Brightwater Logistics, met with Elena Varga in Rotterdam on March 3. Varga runs Northgate Holdings, a shipping broker registered in Cyprus. According to port records, Brightwater Logistics paid Northgate Holdings for three container shipments routed through Antwerp.

Hale later told investigators that he had never heard of Northgate Holdings. She said the payments were routine. The United States Treasury Department opened an inquiry in May.

Daniel Okafor, a former auditor at Brightwater Logistics, reported the payments to the Treasury Department. Okafor worked with Priya Raman, an analyst at the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, to trace the funds. Raman found that Northgate Holdings shared a director with Seaward Trading, a company based in Limassol.

Elena Varga is also the owner of Seaward Trading. In June, Marcus Hale resigned from Brightwater Logistics. The USS Cole Foundation, a veterans charity unrelated to the inquiry, was mentioned in the same filing because it received a donation from Seaward Trading.
